title: Diagnostic lumbar puncture (adult)
indications: Suspected meningitis or encephalitis.
Suspected subarachnoid haemorrhage with negative CT.
Diagnostic work-up of suspected demyelinating or autoimmune neurological disease.

absolute: Clinical signs of raised intracranial pressure or impending herniation.
Infection at the proposed puncture site.

equipment: Three-way tap and manometer for opening pressure.
Four sterile collection tubes (cell count, biochemistry, microbiology, additional).
Local anaesthetic (1% lignocaine) with 5 mL syringe.
consentNotes: Counsel the patient on indication, common side effects (post-dural-puncture headache), serious risks (bleeding, infection, neurological injury, brainstem herniation if unrecognised raised ICP), and alternatives. Document consent.

steps.detail: Review fundoscopy, focal neurology, coagulation. Image first when uncertain.
steps.safetyCheck: STOP if any sign of raised ICP, focal deficit, or recent seizure without imaging.

steps.detail: Left lateral decubitus with knees drawn up and back fully flexed, or seated and leaning forward.
Intercristal line crosses the L4 spinous process; aim for L3–L4 or L4–L5 interspace.
Sterile technique throughout; widely prep the area.
steps.safetyCheck: Confirm sterility of the field before opening the needle.

steps.step: Anaesthetise the skin and deeper tissues
steps.detail: Raise a wheal then infiltrate down toward the interspinous ligament.
Bevel parallel to dural fibres; advance toward the umbilicus until a give signals dural puncture.
Connect the manometer with the patient in the lateral decubitus position with legs extended.
steps.safetyCheck: If pressure > 25 cmH₂O, remove only the minimum CSF needed and escalate.

steps.detail: Fill four tubes (≈ 1–2 mL each) for cell count, biochemistry (protein, glucose; paired serum glucose), microbiology (Gram stain, culture, viral PCR), and storage.
Withdraw with stylet replaced; apply a sterile dressing.

redFlags: New focal neurology or altered consciousness during or after the procedure.
Persistent CSF leak.
Worsening headache with neck stiffness or fever post-procedure.
postProcedureCare: Encourage oral fluids.
Bed rest is no longer routinely required for post-dural-puncture headache prevention.
Document opening pressure and CSF appearance.

complications.management: Hydration, simple analgesia, caffeine; epidural blood patch if persistent and disabling.
Urgent neurosurgical assessment, MRI spine, reversal of anticoagulation as indicated.
Avoid by screening for raised ICP first. If suspected post-procedure, resuscitate, intubate, and seek immediate neurosurgical input.

title: Peripheral IV cannulation (adult)
indications: Intravenous medication or fluid administration.
Blood sampling at the time of cannulation.

absolute: Cellulitis or infection at the chosen site.
relative: Limb with arteriovenous fistula in use for dialysis.
Lymphoedematous or post-mastectomy limb on the affected side.
Burns or skin breakdown at the site.

equipment: Cannula of appropriate gauge (typically 18–20 G for adults).
consentNotes: Explain the procedure, indication, expected sensation, and risks (bruising, infection, infiltration). Verbal consent is usually sufficient.

steps.detail: Standard precautions throughout.
Prefer distal sites first (dorsum of hand → forearm). Avoid joints when possible.
Place 10–15 cm proximal to the chosen vein; do not occlude arterial flow.
steps.safetyCheck: Confirm distal pulse remains palpable.

steps.detail: Single firm wipe; allow to air-dry fully (~30 seconds).
Anchor the vein with the non-dominant hand; insert bevel up at ~15–30°; advance until flashback; then advance the plastic cannula off the stylet.
Discard the stylet immediately into the sharps bin.
steps.safetyCheck: Do not re-sheath needles.

steps.detail: Use 5–10 mL saline; confirm no resistance and no swelling at the site.
Document date, site, and gauge.

redFlags: Bright red pulsatile flashback — suspect arterial cannulation; remove and apply pressure.
Pain on flush, swelling, or pallor — likely infiltration; remove the cannula.
postProcedureCare: Re-site every 72–96 hours or sooner if any sign of phlebitis.
Document each shift with a phlebitis score.

complications.management: Remove cannula; warm compress; consider re-siting on the contralateral limb.
Remove cannula; oral or IV antibiotics per local guideline; review for systemic features.
Withdraw immediately; apply firm pressure for at least 5 minutes; observe for haematoma.

references.label: WHO Best Practices for Injections and Related Procedures Toolkit

title: Wound cleaning and simple interrupted suturing
indications: Clean, recent (< 6–8 hours) laceration not involving deep structures.

absolute: Heavily contaminated bite or puncture wound — clean and leave open.
Suspected tendon, nerve, or vascular injury — refer.
relative: Wound on cosmetically sensitive area (e.g. face) — consider specialist closure.
Significant tissue loss — consider secondary intention or specialist input.

equipment: Skin prep and saline for irrigation.
Local anaesthetic (lignocaine 1%) with adrenaline contraindicated at digits / penis / nose / ears.
Suture material — typically 4-0 to 6-0 non-absorbable monofilament.
consentNotes: Explain wound assessment findings, anaesthetic, expected scar, and risk of infection. Confirm tetanus immunisation status.

steps.detail: Examine for foreign body, tendon, nerve, vascular involvement; document distal neurovascular status.
steps.safetyCheck: STOP and refer if deeper structures are involved or there is uncontrolled bleeding.

steps.detail: Infiltrate the wound edges. Wait at least 5 minutes for full effect.
At least 100 mL of saline per cm of wound; remove all visible debris.
Take equal bites either side; evert the wound edges; space sutures approximately equal to the bite width.
Dry dressing; document wound size, depth, suture count, anaesthetic dose used.

redFlags: Bleeding that does not stop with pressure — suspect arterial involvement.
Loss of distal sensation or motor function after anaesthetic effect should wear off — suspect nerve injury.
postProcedureCare: Keep the wound dry for 48 hours.
Suture removal — face 5 days, scalp 7–10 days, limbs 10–14 days.
Review at 48 hours if any concern for infection.

complications.management: Remove sutures if collection present; clean; oral antibiotics per local guideline.
Re-clean; allow healing by secondary intention or re-suture if early and clean.
Prevent — confirm immunisation status; give tetanus toxoid ± immunoglobulin per protocol.

references.label: Kenya Clinical Guidelines — Minor surgical procedures

title: Urethral urinary catheterisation (adult male)
indications: Acute urinary retention.
Accurate urine output monitoring in critical illness.
Bladder drainage peri-operatively when indicated.

absolute: Suspected urethral trauma (blood at the meatus, perineal haematoma, high-riding prostate).
relative: Recent urological surgery — discuss with the urology team.
Known urethral stricture — anticipate difficulty; consider smaller-gauge catheter or urology input.

equipment: Sterile catheterisation pack with drapes and gloves.
consentNotes: Explain indication, alternatives, expected discomfort, and risks (infection, bleeding, urethral trauma, false passage). Confirm consent and chaperone.

steps.detail: Supine; clean drape; sterile field.

steps.step: Clean the meatus and surrounding skin
steps.detail: Retract the foreskin; clean from meatus outward.
10 mL of lignocaine-chlorhexidine gel into the urethra; allow ≥ 3 minutes for effect.
steps.safetyCheck: Skipping the wait substantially increases pain and urethral trauma.

steps.detail: Hold the penis vertical at first; insert until urine returns plus 2–3 cm more before inflating balloon.
With 10 mL sterile water — only after free urine return.
steps.safetyCheck: STOP and withdraw if inflation causes pain — the balloon may be in the urethra.

steps.detail: Replace the foreskin to prevent paraphimosis.
steps.safetyCheck: Failing to reposition the foreskin is a common, preventable harm.

steps.detail: Insertion difficulty, residual volume, catheter size and date.

redFlags: Bleeding per urethra during the procedure — STOP; suspect false passage.
No urine return despite advancing the catheter into the bladder — verify position before inflating.
postProcedureCare: Hourly output monitoring as clinically indicated.
Daily review for ongoing indication — remove as soon as no longer needed (CAUTI prevention).

complications.management: Remove the catheter if able; collect a culture; treat per local guideline.
Stop; do not re-attempt; refer to urology for cystoscopy-guided catheterisation.
Manual reduction with cold compress; urology referral if irreducible.

references.label: WHO Guidelines on Core Components of Infection Prevention and Control Programmes

title: Basic life support (BLS) — adult
indications: Unresponsive adult with no normal breathing.
Suspected cardiac arrest with no palpable pulse for ≥ 10 sec.

relative: Obvious irreversible death (rigor mortis, dependent lividity).

equipment: Pocket mask / face shield where bystander hesitates direct mouth-to-mouth.
consentNotes: Implied consent applies in unresponsive arrest. Document DNACPR if known.

steps.detail: Shake-shoulders-and-shout. No response → activate emergency response system.
steps.safetyCheck: Confirm scene is safe before approaching.

steps.detail: Head-tilt + chin-lift (jaw-thrust if trauma). Look for chest movement ≤ 10 sec. Agonal gasps count as no breathing.
Lower half of sternum. Depth 5–6 cm. Rate 100–120/min. Allow full chest recoil. Minimise interruptions < 10 sec.
steps.safetyCheck: Hard surface. Compressor's arms straight, shoulders above hands.

steps.detail: Pocket mask / bag-mask 2 breaths of 1-second duration; visible chest rise. Compressions only if untrained / unwilling.

steps.step: Apply AED as soon as available
steps.detail: Pad placement: right of sternum below clavicle + left mid-axillary line. Follow AED prompts. Shock if advised — resume CPR immediately for 2 min before reassessment.
Switch compressor every 2 min to prevent fatigue.

redFlags: ROSC — palpable pulse + signs of life → recovery position + continuous monitoring.
Suspected hypothermia → prolong resuscitation, do not declare death until rewarmed.
Pregnancy in third trimester → manual left uterine displacement + early caesarean if no ROSC by 4 min.
postProcedureCare: Hand over to ALS team with SBAR.
Document time of arrest, witnessed / unwitnessed, downtime, interventions, ROSC.
If ROSC: 12-lead ECG, target SpO₂ 94–98 %, MAP ≥ 65, glucose 6–10, targeted temperature management 32–36 °C.

complications.management: Document; pain relief; do not stop compressions.
Suction; cuffed airway when ALS available.
Decompression + chest drain after ROSC if suspected.

title: Manual defibrillation for shockable rhythm (adult)
indications: Pulseless ventricular tachycardia.
Ventricular fibrillation.

absolute: Wet patient / submerged in water (towel-dry first).
relative: Adherent transdermal medication patch over pad position — remove first.

equipment: Adhesive defibrillation pads (or paddles + conductive gel).
consentNotes: Implied consent in arrest.

steps.detail: Pulseless VT or VF on monitor.
steps.safetyCheck: Compressor steps clear briefly for rhythm check (≤ 5 sec).

steps.detail: Right of sternum below clavicle + left mid-axillary line. Anterior-posterior alternative.
Continue compressions until charged.
steps.safetyCheck: Announce 'STAND CLEAR' before shock.

steps.detail: Confirm no one is touching patient / bed / equipment.
steps.safetyCheck: Confirm rhythm interpretation before each shock.

steps.detail: 2 min compressions BEFORE rhythm reassessment.
After 3rd shock: adrenaline 1 mg IV + amiodarone 300 mg IV. Adrenaline every 3–5 min thereafter; amiodarone 150 mg IV bolus after 5th shock.

redFlags: Pulseless electrical activity (PEA) after shock — search 4 Hs + 4 Ts.
Refractory VF — double sequential defibrillation; consider extracorporeal CPR.
Cardiac tamponade post-defibrillation — pericardiocentesis.
postProcedureCare: Post-ROSC bundle — 12-lead ECG, urgent PCI for STEMI, targeted temperature management.

complications.management: Topical care.
Strict 'stand clear' discipline.
Continue resuscitation; vasopressor / inotrope post-ROSC.

title: Bag-mask ventilation (adult)
indications: Apnoea / inadequate breathing.
Pre-oxygenation before intubation.
Bridge to advanced airway.

relative: Suspected full stomach — high aspiration risk.

consentNotes: Implied consent in emergency.

steps.detail: Head-tilt chin-lift OR jaw-thrust (suspected C-spine). Insert OP / NP airway if tolerated.
Mask covers nose + mouth without overlying eyes. Two-handed technique preferred (C-E grip).
10 breaths/min (every 6 sec) over 1 sec each; tidal volume 6–7 mL/kg ideal body weight. Visible chest rise.
steps.safetyCheck: Avoid hyperventilation (raises intrathoracic pressure → reduces CO + cerebral perfusion).

steps.detail: Mask reseat — Reposition airway — Suction — Open mouth — Pressure (increase) — Alternative airway (LMA / intubation / surgical).

redFlags: Gastric distension → aspiration risk; place NG tube.
Hypoxia despite ventilation → advance to definitive airway.
postProcedureCare: Transition to definitive airway when possible.
Document time, oxygen %, ventilation pressures, response.

complications.management: Cricoid pressure (debated), NG decompression, early definitive airway.
Decompression if tension.

title: Intraosseous (IO) access — adult / paediatric
indications: Failed IV access × 2 attempts (or 90 sec) in life-threatening situation.
Cardiac arrest first-line vascular access.
Severe shock / status epilepticus where IV unobtainable.

absolute: Recent IO at same site within 48 h.

equipment: EZ-IO drill (preferred) OR manual IO needle.
Lidocaine 40 mg (2 % 2 mL) for conscious patient.
consentNotes: Implied consent in life-threatening emergency.

steps.detail: Proximal humerus (preferred adult, high flow), proximal tibia, distal tibia (paediatric), distal femur, sternum.
Chlorhexidine 2 % single firm wipe.
Perpendicular to bone; advance with drill 90° to surface until loss of resistance ('pop') felt; needle stands up unsupported.
steps.safetyCheck: Pink-colour catheter for adult; blue for paediatric (longer).

steps.detail: Aspirate marrow (bonus — not always possible). Flush with 10 mL saline + observe for extravasation.
Inject 40 mg (2 mL of 2 %) lidocaine SLOWLY over 2 min into IO line — counsel burning sensation. Wait 60 sec before infusion.
Pressure bag for rapid infusion (gravity inadequate). ANY drug or fluid that can be given IV can be given IO.

redFlags: Extravasation → compartment syndrome (rare but serious).
Failure to flow despite flush → reposition / replace.
Compartment syndrome — pain, swelling, pulselessness.
postProcedureCare: Replace with peripheral IV / central line within 24 h.
Remove IO needle on standard withdrawal once IV established.
Document site, time, flow rate.

complications.management: Remove needle; orthopaedic input; fasciotomy if compartment syndrome confirmed.
Rare (< 1 % with sterile technique + < 24 h dwell time). Antibiotic per culture.
Imaging; orthopaedic referral; alternative access.

title: Internal jugular central venous catheter — ultrasound-guided
indications: Need for vasopressor / inotrope infusion.
Failed peripheral IV access in sepsis / shock.
Central venous pressure monitoring.
Long-term IV antibiotics / chemotherapy / parenteral nutrition.
Renal replacement therapy access.

absolute: Anticoagulated + uncontrolled bleeding (IJ preferred over subclavian).
relative: Severe COPD / contralateral pneumothorax (subclavian — choose IJ).

equipment: Sterile gown + drape + gloves + mask + cap.
consentNotes: Counsel risks: pneumothorax (lower in IJ vs subclavian), arterial puncture, infection, line-related thrombosis, air embolism, arrhythmia. Document written consent.

steps.detail: Trendelenburg 10–15 ° head-down (engorges vein), head turned slightly away.
steps.safetyCheck: Pulse oximetry + ECG monitor; sterile barrier precautions (gown, drape, gloves, mask, cap, eye protection).

steps.detail: Vein collapses with pressure; artery pulsatile. Right IJ preferred (straighter course to SVC, no thoracic duct).
Wide chlorhexidine prep; full sterile drape.
1 % lignocaine 5–10 mL infiltrated skin + deeper.

steps.step: Cannulate vein under direct ultrasound vision
steps.detail: Advance needle, aim for vessel centre, draw back to confirm dark non-pulsatile blood.
steps.safetyCheck: If pulsatile / bright-red blood → arterial. Withdraw + apply 5 min pressure.

steps.detail: Pass guidewire ≥ 20 cm; remove needle; nick skin; pass dilator; pass catheter over wire; remove wire.
Aspirate + flush all lumens. Stop catheter tip at upper SVC / right atrium junction. CXR to confirm + exclude pneumothorax.
steps.safetyCheck: Tip should NOT be in heart chamber (arrhythmia).

steps.detail: Stitch in 3 places. Transparent dressing. Document depth + date.

redFlags: Carotid puncture — sustained pressure 10 min, vascular surgical referral if uncontrolled bleeding.
Pneumothorax / haemothorax on post-line CXR → chest drain.
Cardiac arrhythmia — withdraw wire if induces arrhythmia.
Air embolism — sudden cardiopulmonary collapse — left lateral Trendelenburg; 100 % O₂; aspirate air via line.
postProcedureCare: CXR within 1 h.
Chlorhexidine + transparent dressing change every 7 days.
Aseptic line-access technique each time.
Daily review of necessity — REMOVE WHEN NO LONGER NEEDED (CLABSI prevention).

complications.management: Chest drain if symptomatic / progressing. Conservative if small + asymptomatic.
5–10 min sustained pressure. Vascular surgery if bleeding uncontrolled / haematoma expanding.
Remove line if confirmed line-source bacteraemia; targeted antibiotic.
Doppler USS; anticoagulate; remove line if persistent / extending.

title: Paracentesis — diagnostic + therapeutic (adult)
indications: New ascites — diagnostic.
Suspected spontaneous bacterial peritonitis (SBP).
Therapeutic large-volume paracentesis for symptomatic tense ascites.

relative: INR > 2 / platelets < 20 (cirrhotic patients usually tolerate without correction).

equipment: Therapeutic kit: pigtail catheter + drainage bag.
Sample tubes: cell count + biochemistry + albumin + culture + cytology + Gram stain.
Albumin 20 % for replacement (8 g per L drained).
consentNotes: Counsel: bleeding, peritonitis, bowel perforation, persistent leak. Document written consent.

steps.detail: Supine, slight left lateral tilt. Empty bladder.
steps.safetyCheck: Ultrasound to localise + measure depth; mark site.

steps.detail: Preferred left lower quadrant — 2-finger-breadth medial + cephalad to anterior superior iliac spine. AVOID rectus muscle (epigastric vessels), surgical scars, bowel-loop visible on USS.
Chlorhexidine wide. Sterile drape.
Wheal + deeper infiltration; aspirate as advancing to confirm ascitic fluid.

Insert 22-G needle perpendicular; advance with Z-track (pulled skin) to reduce post-procedure leak; aspirate 20–60 mL. Send: cell count + diff, total protein + albumin, glucose, LDH, amylase, Gram stain + culture (bedside-inoculated blood culture bottles), cytology, AFB / TB PCR if indicated.
steps.safetyCheck: Ascitic neutrophils ≥ 250/mm³ → SBP — empirical IV ceftriaxone.

steps.detail: Pigtail catheter into ascites — drain by gravity. Max 4–5 L if no albumin replacement; otherwise drain to dryness with albumin 8 g per L drained > 5 L.
steps.safetyCheck: Stop if severe abdominal pain, sudden hypotension.

steps.detail: Apply pressure 5 min. Transparent dressing.

redFlags: Persistent fluid leak post-procedure → stoma bag + pressure dressing; may resolve spontaneously.
Hypotension during / after drainage — paracentesis-induced circulatory dysfunction; IV albumin + ITU.
Bowel perforation — peritonitis, raised CRP, free air → surgery.
postProcedureCare: Albumin 8 g per L drained > 5 L.
Monitor BP + Na + creatinine 24 h.
Diuretic adjustment per fluid balance.

complications.management: Always send neutrophil count + culture in any new ascites.
Stop drainage, urgent surgical referral, cross-match.
Albumin replacement, terlipressin if HRS established.

title: Thoracocentesis — diagnostic / therapeutic pleural effusion
indications: Diagnostic of new pleural effusion.
Therapeutic drainage of symptomatic effusion.
Suspected empyema / parapneumonic effusion.
equipment: 16–18 G IV cannula or pigtail catheter.
60 mL syringe + three-way tap + drainage bag.
consentNotes: Counsel: pneumothorax (5–10 %), haemorrhage, infection, re-expansion pulmonary oedema. Written consent.

steps.detail: Sit forward over a table with arms folded on pillow.
Posterior 'triangle of safety' — typically 1–2 intercostal spaces below upper border of effusion in mid-scapular line. Mark; measure depth.
steps.safetyCheck: Avoid below 9th rib (risk diaphragm / liver / spleen).

steps.detail: Wide chlorhexidine, sterile drape.
Infiltrate skin → rib → pleura, walking the needle OVER the upper edge of the rib below (avoid neurovascular bundle which sits UNDER the upper rib).
Pierce above rib aiming perpendicular. Aspirate as advancing to confirm fluid. Once fluid obtained, advance the cannula off needle into pleural space.

Diagnostic: 50 mL — send for cell count + diff, biochemistry (Light's criteria: protein, LDH; paired serum), pH (within minutes of sampling), culture, Gram stain, cytology, AFB / ADA if TB suspected. Therapeutic: drain slowly — max 1.5 L per session to reduce RPE.
Apply sterile dressing.

redFlags: Sudden cough or dyspnoea during drainage — stop; observe for pneumothorax / RPE.
Bright-red bloody aspirate — possibly artery (intercostal / IMA); apply pressure + cardiothoracic input.
Diaphragmatic / abdominal puncture — surgical assessment.
postProcedureCare: CXR within 1 h to exclude pneumothorax.
If empyema: chest drain instead of repeat aspirations.
Send fluid pH < 7.2 OR pus → chest drain + IV antibiotics.

complications.management: Small + asymptomatic — observe + repeat CXR 4–6 h. Large / symptomatic — chest drain.
Drain slowly (max 1.5 L/session); supportive O₂, diuretic if mild, mechanical ventilation if severe.
Always send pH + glucose + LDH + Gram stain; treat empyema with chest drain + IV antibiotics.

title: Chest drain insertion (intercostal catheter) — adult
indications: Tension pneumothorax (after needle decompression).
Spontaneous pneumothorax — large / symptomatic.
Haemothorax.
Empyema / large parapneumonic effusion.
Persistent / large pleural effusion.
equipment: Chest drain (small-bore Seldinger 12 Fr usual; large-bore for haemothorax).
consentNotes: Counsel: bleeding, lung injury, infection, persistent air leak, organ injury. Written consent in non-emergency.

steps.detail: Patient supine with arm behind head. Triangle of safety (anterior border latissimus dorsi, lateral border pectoralis major, line above 5th intercostal space, apex axilla). Typically 5th ICS mid-axillary line.
steps.safetyCheck: Confirm side from CXR + clinical examination before draping.

steps.detail: Chlorhexidine wide, sterile drape.
Walk over upper rib to pleura; large volume (10–20 mL 1 % lignocaine) — pleura is exquisitely sensitive.

Small skin incision above upper border of rib. Insert introducer needle into pleural cavity, aspirating until fluid / air obtained. Pass guidewire — never advance with resistance. Dilate sequentially. Pass chest drain over wire.
steps.safetyCheck: Trocar technique (blunt dissection blunt-tip catheter) for large drain in haemothorax — NEVER push trocar through chest wall blindly.

steps.detail: Drain must be below patient's chest level. Confirm swing (respiratory variation) + bubbling (air leak) / drainage.
Stitch in 'mattress' or 'purse-string' suture to hold drain + close on removal. Adhesive dressing. Document depth at skin.

redFlags: Continued large air leak after 5 days → bronchopleural fistula; surgical referral.
Sudden surgical emphysema spreading → kink / blocked drain; review immediately.
Massive haemothorax > 1.5 L on insertion / > 200 mL/h × 4 h → urgent thoracotomy.
Subcutaneous emphysema → drain blockage or displacement.
postProcedureCare: Erect CXR within 1 h to confirm position + lung re-expansion.
Monitor swing + bubbling + drainage 4-hourly.
Remove when: (a) no swing / bubble for 24 h, (b) lung fully expanded on CXR, (c) drainage < 200 mL/24 h.

complications.management: CT chest; thoracic surgery.
Surgical exploration; correct any coagulopathy.
Withdraw + reinsert OR replace; do NOT advance further.
Clamp drain briefly + supportive care.

title: Needle thoracostomy — tension pneumothorax
indications: Suspected tension pneumothorax (hypotension + respiratory distress + unilateral hyper-resonance + tracheal deviation + reduced air entry).

relative: Simple pneumothorax without tension features — proceed to formal chest drain instead.

equipment: Sterile alcohol wipe (no time for full prep in true emergency).
consentNotes: Implied consent — life-threatening emergency.

steps.detail: Traditional 2nd intercostal space mid-clavicular line OR 5th ICS mid-axillary line (preferred — adequate chest wall depth; misses mediastinum).
Above upper border of 3rd rib (or 5th rib for axillary approach). Advance until hiss of air / rush.
steps.safetyCheck: If no hiss in suspected tension — re-evaluate diagnosis; do NOT keep advancing.

steps.detail: Tape cannula in place.
Needle thoracostomy is TEMPORISING — formal chest drain insertion immediately after as definitive treatment.

redFlags: No improvement after needle thoracostomy → reconsider diagnosis (haemothorax, cardiac tamponade, PE).
Massive subcutaneous emphysema → revisit drain position.
postProcedureCare: Erect CXR after chest drain.
Document time + indication + immediate response.

complications.management: Use longer 14-G cannula (8 cm), or proceed direct to chest drain.
Apply pressure; chest drain may help by evacuating blood.

title: Urinary catheterisation (urethral) — adult
indications: Acute urinary retention.
Strict urine output measurement (critically ill / peri-operative).
Bladder washout.
Drug instillation (intravesical chemotherapy).
Investigation of post-void residual / video-urodynamics.

absolute: Suspected urethral injury (pelvic trauma, blood at meatus, scrotal haematoma, high-riding prostate).
relative: Recent urological surgery — discuss with team.

equipment: Foley catheter appropriate size (Ch 12–14 standard adult; larger for haematuria).
10 mL syringe + 10 mL water for balloon.
consentNotes: Consent + chaperone offer.

steps.detail: Wash hands; gloves + apron; clean trolley.
Female: supine knees flexed apart. Male: supine. Clean meatus + surrounding tissue with saline-soaked gauze.
Instil 10 mL of 2 % lignocaine gel into urethra; wait 2 min for effect (especially men).
Female: 5–7 cm. Male: advance fully to hub before inflating balloon. NEVER force.
steps.safetyCheck: Stop + reassess if pain / resistance. Withdraw if no urine flow at expected depth.

steps.detail: 10 mL sterile water (NOT saline — crystallises). Withdraw gently until balloon engages bladder neck.
Secure catheter to inner thigh / abdomen with adhesive holder. Connect to drainage bag below bladder level.

redFlags: Failure to pass — STOP, do not force. Try smaller catheter, suprapubic, or urology.
Bright-red bleeding after insertion — false passage / urethral injury.
No urine after balloon inflation — confirm placement (USS bladder), do NOT deflate balloon if in correct position.
Post-obstruction diuresis — replace fluid losses + monitor electrolytes.
postProcedureCare: Document indication, type, size, date + time, urine appearance + volume.
Daily review of need — remove ASAP (CAUTI prevention).
Clean meatus daily with soap + water.

complications.management: Stop, urology referral, may need suprapubic catheter.
Remove if possible; culture-guided antibiotic for symptomatic infection only (do NOT treat asymptomatic bacteriuria).
Antimuscarinic (oxybutynin) short-term.

title: Nasogastric tube insertion (adult / child)
indications: Gastric decompression (obstruction, ileus, pancreatitis).
Enteral feeding (short-term).
Drug administration where oral route unavailable.
Lavage in selected poisoning.
consentNotes: Counsel: discomfort, gagging, possible insertion into airway, malposition risks. Verbal consent if conscious.

steps.detail: Tip of nose → earlobe → xiphisternum. Mark insertion length on tube.

Patient sitting upright with chin to chest (closes airway). Insert through nostril, advance straight back along floor of nasal cavity. When tip reaches oropharynx, ask patient to swallow sips of water.

(1) Aspirate gastric contents + pH ≤ 5.5 (preferred). (2) Chest X-ray if pH unobtainable or for ICU / unconscious patient (mandatory NG-feed before first use). NEVER use auscultation alone (whoosh test) — unreliable.
steps.safetyCheck: DO NOT FEED OR ADMINISTER DRUGS until position confirmed safe (pH ≤ 5.5 or CXR shows tip below diaphragm).

steps.detail: Tape to nose + cheek. Document length at nose / external markers.

redFlags: Coughing / cyanosis / inability to phonate → airway placement; WITHDRAW IMMEDIATELY.
Resistance + bleeding → false passage; stop + reassess.
Confused / sedated patient with new feed-related desaturation → check tube position (Never Event in UK NHS — feed into lung).
postProcedureCare: Re-check position before each feed / drug administration.
Aspirate hourly for residual gastric volume on feed.
Replace tube every 4–6 weeks (fine-bore feeding tube) per local protocol.

complications.management: Withdraw immediately. CXR + supportive care.
Alternate nostrils; consider PEG for long-term feeding.
Confirm tube position; head-of-bed 30°; antibiotics if confirmed.

references.label: NHS England NPSA Alert: Nasogastric tube safety

title: Intrauterine device (copper or levonorgestrel) insertion
indications: Long-acting reversible contraception (LARC) — 5–10 years (Cu-IUD) / 3–8 years (LNG-IUD).
Emergency contraception within 5 days of unprotected sex (Cu-IUD only — most effective EC).
Heavy menstrual bleeding (LNG-IUD).

absolute: Distorted uterine cavity (large fibroid, septate uterus).
relative: Severely retroverted / anteverted uterus (use careful technique).

equipment: IUD device (Cu-380A copper; LNG 52 mg or 19.5 mg).
consentNotes: Counsel risks (perforation 1–2/1000, expulsion 5 %, infection in first 3 weeks, irregular bleeding initially, ectopic if pregnancy occurs). Document written consent + STI screen result.

steps.detail: LMP within last 7 days OR negative pregnancy test OR continuous reliable contraception.
Chlamydia + gonorrhoea NAAT before / at insertion (treat positive results).
Identify cervix; check uterine position + size + tenderness.
Antiseptic prep (chlorhexidine / povidone-iodine).
Grasp anterior cervix with tenaculum; pass uterine sound to fundus + measure length (typical 6–9 cm; min 6 cm for IUD).
Load device, advance through cervix to fundus, release. Withdraw inserter slowly.
Cut at 2–3 cm from cervix; document length.

redFlags: Severe pain / vasovagal collapse — atropine + IV fluid + lie flat.
Suspected perforation (sudden loss of resistance / unable to feel device) — stop, USS, refer.
Bleeding more than expected — examine for cervical / vaginal injury.
Subsequent pregnancy with IUD in situ — exclude ectopic + remove device if threads visible.
postProcedureCare: Counsel: irregular bleeding 3–6 months (especially Cu); 30 % amenorrhoea on LNG at 1 year.
Self-check threads monthly.
Follow-up at 6 weeks for thread check.
Return for new severe pain, fever, abnormal bleeding, dyspareunia, partner can feel threads.

complications.management: USS to localise; laparoscopy if intra-abdominal; emergency contraception in interim.
Ceftriaxone 500 mg IM + doxycycline 100 mg BID × 14 days + metronidazole 400 mg BID × 14 days. IUD does NOT need routine removal.
Confirm with USS; reinsert at next menstrual period.

references.label: WHO Medical Eligibility Criteria for Contraceptive Use

title: Manual vacuum aspiration (MVA) — incomplete abortion / MTOP completion
indications: Incomplete spontaneous miscarriage with retained products.
Failed medical management of missed / incomplete miscarriage.
Surgical termination of pregnancy ≤ 12 weeks.
Retained products of conception postpartum.

relative: Severe anaemia (transfuse first if heavy bleeding).

equipment: Sterile MVA syringe (60 mL Ipas) + cannulae 4–12 mm.
consentNotes: Counsel: bleeding, pain, perforation, infection, retained products, anaesthetic risk. Document written consent + post-procedure contraception plan.

steps.detail: USS, FBC, blood group + Rh, STI screen. Treat infection before procedure where feasible.
Paracervical block — 10 mL of 1 % lignocaine at 3 + 9 o'clock positions on cervix. Add PO ibuprofen 400 mg + sublingual misoprostol 400 µg 1–3 h pre-procedure for cervical priming if > 9 weeks.
Antiseptic prep. Grasp anterior cervix.
Confirm direction + length (gentle technique to avoid perforation).
Sequential dilators to size of cannula required (cannula size = gestational weeks in mm).
Insert cannula attached to charged MVA syringe; rotate 180° back-and-forth covering all uterine walls. Continue until: no more tissue, gritty sensation, foamy red discharge only.
steps.safetyCheck: Inspect aspirated tissue — confirm products of conception (villi, decidua). If absent, refer urology / gynaecology — possible ectopic.

steps.detail: Confirm uterus empty by repeat USS where available.

redFlags: Severe pain / haemorrhage / shock → uterotonic + crystalloid + cross-match + theatre.
Sudden loss of resistance + free air on USS → uterine perforation, laparoscopy / laparotomy.
Absence of villi → suspect ectopic; serial β-hCG.
postProcedureCare: Observe 30–60 min for bleeding + pain.
Counsel: bleeding 1–2 weeks; menses return 4–8 weeks; avoid intercourse / tampons / bath for 1 week.
Anti-D 250 IU IM if Rh-negative > 10 weeks.
Start contraception same day (IUD insertion immediate).
Emotional support; mental-health screening.

complications.management: Stop procedure; laparoscopy; oxytocin.
Tamponade + suture; uterotonic.
Antibiotic + repeat MVA / D&C if persistent.
Hysteroscopic adhesiolysis.

title: Manual removal of retained placenta
indications: Retained placenta > 30 min after delivery despite active management.
PPH with retained placenta.
consentNotes: Counsel: requires general / regional anaesthesia, risk of bleeding, infection, uterine inversion. Verbal consent in emergency.

steps.detail: IV access × 2. 1 L crystalloid bolus. Cross-match 4 units.
Regional (spinal) preferred; general anaesthesia if shocked. Inhaled nitrous oxide if no anaesthetist.
Catheterise.
Sterile gown to elbow. Trace umbilical cord with one hand outside abdomen pushing fundus down. Other hand follows cord through cervix.
steps.safetyCheck: Identify cleavage plane between placenta + uterine wall — DO NOT pull on cord (risk inversion or partial separation).

steps.detail: Use side of hand to develop plane between placenta + decidua. Detach completely, then carefully remove with fingers behind placenta. Inspect cotyledons + membranes — must be complete.
External hand on abdomen, internal hand massages uterus. IV oxytocin 10 IU bolus + 40 IU in 500 mL infusion. Add ergometrine / carboprost / TXA as needed (see PPH ladder).

redFlags: Placenta accreta / increta / percreta — abnormal absence of cleavage plane → STOP, hysterectomy or uterine artery embolisation, multidisciplinary team.
Continued haemorrhage despite full uterotonic ladder → laparotomy / hysterectomy.
Uterine inversion — recognise (fundus not palpable abdominally, mass in vagina) → emergency replacement under anaesthesia.
postProcedureCare: IV antibiotics — single dose cefazolin 2 g or amoxicillin-clavulanate.
Continue oxytocin infusion 8–12 h post-procedure.
Monitor lochia + uterine tone hourly first 2 h, then 4-hourly.
Cross-match + group + Hb 4 h post + 24 h.

complications.management: Full PPH ladder; tamponade balloon; surgery if persistent.
IV ampicillin + gentamicin + metronidazole.
Manual replacement under anaesthesia + uterotonic; laparotomy if failed.

title: Wound suturing — simple laceration
indications: Clean linear laceration < 12 h old (24 h face / scalp).
Cosmetically significant facial laceration.
Tendon / nerve / vessel intact, no foreign body.

absolute: Heavily contaminated / animal bite (delayed primary closure).

equipment: Local anaesthetic (1 % lignocaine ± adrenaline; AVOID adrenaline on digits / pinna / nose / penis).
Suture material (size depending on site — face 5/0 or 6/0; trunk / limb 3/0 or 4/0).
consentNotes: Counsel: scarring, infection, suture-removal need + timing, tetanus status. Verbal consent for simple lacerations.

steps.detail: Examine for tendon / nerve / vessel / joint involvement. Check distal function + sensation BEFORE anaesthetic. X-ray if FB suspected.
Inject 1 % lignocaine into wound edge from inside (less painful) until skin blanches; wait 5 min.
100–200 mL warmed sterile saline under pressure (with syringe + 18 G needle). Removes most contamination.
Remove devitalised tissue + foreign material.
Simple interrupted sutures: enter 5 mm from edge, perpendicular, equal depth both sides. Tie 3 throws for monofilament, 4 for braided. Space sutures by twice the bite depth.
Antibiotic ointment optional (no clear evidence). Cover with sterile non-adherent dressing.

redFlags: Open joint / tendon / nerve injury → refer specialist / theatre.
Heavy contamination → delayed primary closure after 3–5 days saline-soaked packing.
Animal / human bite → leave open + antibiotic; tetanus / rabies prophylaxis as indicated.
Signs of infection at follow-up — pus, erythema, fever → remove some sutures + antibiotic + culture.
postProcedureCare: Keep dry 24–48 h.
Suture removal: face 5 days, scalp 7–10 days, trunk / limbs 10–14 days, joints 14 days.
Tetanus prophylaxis per WHO criteria.
Return for fever, increasing pain / redness, pus, or signs of poor healing.

complications.management: Remove some sutures, drain pus, antibiotic + culture.
Cleanse, re-suture if early; secondary intention if late.
Silicone sheets, intralesional steroid; refer plastics if severe.
Removal + drainage.

title: Incision + drainage of cutaneous abscess
indications: Fluctuant cutaneous / subcutaneous abscess.
Symptomatic abscess (severe pain, cellulitis, fever).

relative: Adjacent to nerve / vessel (e.g. face triangle of danger) — image first.

consentNotes: Counsel: pain, bleeding, scarring, need for packing + dressing changes, possible antibiotic. Verbal consent.

steps.detail: Pre-incisional aspiration with 18-G needle if uncertain — pus confirms diagnosis. Ultrasound for deep abscess.
Chlorhexidine; sterile drape.
Field block AROUND abscess (anaesthetic injected into purulent area is ineffective + spreads infection).
Stab incision over the most fluctuant point along skin tension lines (Langer's). Adequate length (≥ 1.5 cm for typical abscess) to allow drainage + packing.
Express pus. Send aerobic + anaerobic culture. Break up loculi with forceps. Irrigate with sterile saline.
Iodoform ribbon or saline-soaked gauze. Do NOT pack tightly. Leave 1–2 cm protruding.
Sterile gauze + tape.

redFlags: Significant cellulitis / systemic features → IV antibiotics + admit.
Diabetic / immunocompromised → broader antibiotic + admit.
Necrotising-fasciitis features (pain disproportionate, crepitus, bullae) → SURGICAL EMERGENCY.
MRSA prevalence — covering antibiotic where high-risk patient.
postProcedureCare: Dressing change at 24 h then daily until healed.
Reduce / remove packing at follow-up review.
Antibiotic — NOT routinely required after I+D unless: surrounding cellulitis > 2 cm, systemic features, immunocompromise, face / hand, MRSA risk.

complications.management: Re-incise; deeper exploration; imaging.
Oral flucloxacillin / amoxicillin-clavulanate.
Blood cultures + IV antibiotics + admit.

title: Emergency cricothyroidotomy (can't intubate, can't oxygenate)
indications: Failed intubation + failed bag-mask ventilation + falling oxygenation ('CICO' scenario).
equipment: Cuffed tracheostomy tube size 6.0 (adult) — OR 6.0 ETT cut to 15 cm.
consentNotes: Implied consent in life-threatening emergency.

steps.detail: Patient supine + head extended. Identify cricothyroid membrane (depression between thyroid cartilage above + cricoid cartilage below — 1 finger-breadth below thyroid prominence).
Non-dominant hand stabilises larynx between thumb + middle finger; index finger palpates membrane.
If anatomy unclear: 4 cm vertical incision through skin, blunt-dissect down to membrane.
steps.safetyCheck: Avoid sweeping medial; bleeding from anterior jugular veins controlled by digital pressure.

steps.detail: Insert scalpel horizontally through cricothyroid membrane; rotate 90° to enlarge.
Pass bougie through stab + into trachea (clicks felt); rail tracheal tube over bougie.
Inflate cuff; ventilate via bag; confirm bilateral air entry + ETCO₂ + chest rise.

redFlags: Inability to identify landmarks → vertical skin incision + palpate.
Tracheal injury / posterior wall perforation → urgent surgical airway team.
Massive haemorrhage → digital pressure; surgical exploration.
postProcedureCare: Definitive surgical airway / formal tracheostomy by ENT / cardiothoracic team within 24 h.
CXR to confirm tube position + exclude pneumothorax / mediastinitis.
Antibiotic prophylaxis controversial.

complications.management: Needle cricothyroidotomy + jet ventilation as backup.
Digital pressure; surgery.
ENT follow-up.

title: 12-lead ECG recording
indications: Chest pain workup.
Arrhythmia detection.
Pre-operative assessment.
Routine screening in some contexts (sport, drug initiation).

relative: Severely uncooperative patient (sedation may be needed for accurate trace).

equipment: Skin preparation (alcohol wipe; shave if hairy).
consentNotes: Verbal consent.

steps.detail: Supine, chest fully exposed, relaxed. Quiet environment.
Clean skin with alcohol; shave hair if needed. Allow to dry.
RA right arm, LA left arm, RL right leg, LL left leg. Position on wrists / ankles or proximal limbs.
V1 4th ICS R sternal edge. V2 4th ICS L sternal edge. V4 5th ICS mid-clavicular line. V3 between V2 + V4. V5 5th ICS anterior axillary line. V6 5th ICS mid-axillary line.
Standard 12-lead 10-sec trace. Add rhythm strip if arrhythmia. Posterior leads (V7–V9) + right-sided (V4R) if inferior STEMI / suspect posterior MI.
Rate, rhythm, axis, intervals (PR, QRS, QT/QTc), ST segments, T waves, P waves. Compare to previous if available.

redFlags: STEMI pattern → cath lab activation + dual antiplatelet + statin + heparin.
Complete heart block / Mobitz II → transcutaneous pacing standby.
QTc > 500 ms → withdraw QT drugs + electrolyte correction.
Brugada / WPW / long-QT — counsel + electrophysiology referral.
postProcedureCare: File electronically + paper backup.
Comparison with prior tracings essential for interpretation.

complications.management: Repeat with correct positioning; key lesson — review chest landmarks before connecting.
Hypoallergenic alternative.

title: Peak expiratory flow rate (PEFR) measurement
indications: Diagnose + monitor asthma.
Assess severity of acute exacerbation.
Track response to bronchodilator + ICS therapy.

relative: Severe respiratory distress — perform after stabilisation.

consentNotes: Verbal consent.

steps.detail: Standing or sitting upright. Reset meter to zero.
Take deep breath in to total lung capacity.
No tongue in mouthpiece.
Short sharp blast — peak achieved in first 100 ms.
steps.safetyCheck: Do not exhale slowly (forced vital capacity manoeuvre — different test).

steps.detail: Three attempts within 30 s of each other; record the highest.
Predicted values by sex, age, height. > 80 % personal best = good control. 50–80 % = moderate exacerbation. < 50 % = severe; < 33 % = life-threatening.

redFlags: < 33 % predicted / personal best — life-threatening asthma; admit + IV magnesium + intensive care.
postProcedureCare: Issue patient home peak-flow meter for monitoring.
Set personal best after 2 weeks of recording.

complications.management: Demonstrate again + repeat after good inspiration + sharp blow.

title: Otoscopy — ear examination
indications: Ear pain.
Hearing loss.
Ear discharge.
Vertigo workup.
Routine ear screening in children.

relative: Heavily impacted wax obscuring view — softening drops first.

equipment: Wax-removal kit (loop / forceps / suction) if obstructive wax.
consentNotes: Verbal consent.

steps.detail: Look for swelling, erythema, discharge, lesions.
Largest size that fits comfortably.
Up + back (adult); down + back (child < 3) to straighten the ear canal.
steps.safetyCheck: Hand resting on cheek so movement of head moves whole hand with otoscope.

steps.detail: Gently insert + advance until tympanic membrane visualised. Sweep around to view entire drum.
Cone of light (anterior-inferior quadrant), umbo, handle of malleus, pars tensa + pars flaccida. Note colour, integrity, mobility on pneumatic otoscopy where available.

redFlags: Cholesteatoma (white keratin pearl in pars flaccida) → ENT referral.
Tympanic perforation with discharge → CSOM pathway.
Foreign body — particularly batteries (urgent removal).
Bulging erythematous drum + reduced mobility → AOM.
postProcedureCare: Clean speculum or dispose.
Document findings: 'normal landmarks', 'pearly grey', 'mobile' etc.

complications.management: Stop, observe healing.

title: Direct ophthalmoscopy (fundoscopy)
indications: Headache workup (papilloedema).
Hypertension / diabetes review.
Visual symptoms.
Stroke evaluation.

absolute: Suspected acute angle-closure glaucoma — DO NOT dilate.
relative: Significant cataract obstructing view — refer ophthalmology.

equipment: Mydriatic drops (tropicamide 0.5–1 %) — optional + only after assessing acuity + IOP risk.
consentNotes: Verbal consent for mydriatic + advise on transient blurred vision / not to drive 6 h.

steps.detail: Reduce ambient light for better pupil dilation + visualisation.
Patient seated, fixed on distant point. Examiner same eye-to-eye (right examines right; left examines left).
From 30 cm; both eyes simultaneously. Absent reflex → cataract / retinal detachment / retinoblastoma (urgent).
steps.safetyCheck: Compare reflex between two eyes.

steps.detail: Move closer maintaining red reflex; rotate dial to focus on retina (+ lenses for hyperopia, − for myopia).
Follow blood vessels back to disc. Examine: optic disc (margins, colour, cup-to-disc ratio, papilloedema), vessels (AV ratio, nipping, exudates), macula.

redFlags: Papilloedema → urgent neuro-imaging (raised ICP, mass).
Retinal haemorrhage / cotton-wool spots / hard exudates → systemic disease (hypertension, diabetes, vasculitis).
Pale optic disc (atrophy) → previous ischaemia / compression / glaucoma.
Roth spot (white-centred haemorrhage) → endocarditis / leukaemia.
postProcedureCare: Document findings + draw image.
Counsel about blurred vision for 6 h after mydriatic.

complications.management: Urgent ophthalmology + IOP-lowering treatment.

title: Capillary blood glucose — finger-prick
indications: Suspected hypo / hyperglycaemia.
Diabetes monitoring.
Sick-day + screening.

relative: Infection at finger site — use alternative site.

consentNotes: Verbal consent.

steps.detail: Wash with soap + water; if cold finger, ask patient to warm in lukewarm water.
Insert strip; check code matches strip batch (modern meters auto-code).
Side of finger pulp (less sensitive than tip). Avoid thumb / index finger if frequent use. Alternate fingers.
Use side of finger; squeeze gently. Discard first drop (interstitial fluid contamination).
Touch strip to blood drop; capillary fill. Wait for result (5 sec). Apply pressure to finger.
Normal fasting 4.0–6.0 mmol/L; post-meal < 7.8. Hypoglycaemia < 4.0 (treat); hyperglycaemia > 11.0.

redFlags: Glucose < 3.0 mmol/L symptomatic → treat hypoglycaemia.
Glucose > 25 mmol/L → confirm with venous; check ketones; DKA / HHS workup.
postProcedureCare: Document result in chart.
Apply gauze to finger.
Dispose lancet in sharps bin.

complications.management: Repeat with fresh strip; confirm with venous lab if uncertain.

title: Focused Assessment with Sonography in Trauma (FAST / e-FAST)
indications: Blunt abdominal / chest trauma.
Penetrating thoraco-abdominal trauma.
Unexplained hypotension in trauma.
Sudden cardiovascular collapse (PEA arrest — exclude tamponade / pneumothorax / RV strain).
equipment: Portable ultrasound with curvilinear (2–5 MHz) + linear (5–10 MHz for e-FAST pleural views).
consentNotes: Implied consent in emergency.

steps.detail: Curvilinear probe, mid-axillary line at 10–11th rib. Look for anechoic fluid stripe between liver + right kidney.
Probe more posterior + cephalad than RUQ. Fluid above / around spleen + spleen-kidney space.
Suprapubic, sagittal + transverse. Anechoic fluid posterior to bladder.
Probe pointed cephalad under xiphoid. Anechoic fluid around heart in pericardial space. Useful for cardiac arrest pathway.
Linear probe anterior 2nd intercostal space midclavicular bilaterally. Identify pleural sliding + lung sliding. Absence + 'lung point' suggest pneumothorax.

redFlags: Free fluid in unstable patient → likely haemoperitoneum → immediate laparotomy.
Pericardial effusion + hypotension → tamponade → pericardiocentesis.
Pneumothorax (no lung sliding) → needle thoracostomy / chest drain.
Negative FAST does NOT rule out injury — repeat scan or CT in stable patient.
postProcedureCare: Document images + findings.
Repeat scan if clinical deterioration.

complications.complication: False negative (small bleed, retroperitoneal injury, hollow viscus injury)
complications.management: Maintain clinical suspicion; CT if stable; repeat FAST; serial assessment.

title: Arterial line cannulation — radial artery
indications: Continuous BP monitoring (haemodynamic instability, vasopressor infusion).
Frequent ABG sampling.
Per-operative monitoring.

absolute: Absent radial pulse / poor collateral circulation (Allen test).

equipment: 20-G short cannula or 22-G in slim wrists.
consentNotes: Counsel: thrombosis, infection, distal ischaemia (rare). Verbal consent or part of ICU consent.

steps.detail: Compress radial + ulnar arteries simultaneously, patient closes fist, relax fist, release ulnar — palmar reperfusion within 7 sec confirms collateral flow.
Wrist hyperextended over rolled towel; abducted.
Chlorhexidine, sterile drape.
1 % lignocaine 1 mL skin wheal.
Palpate radial pulse; insert cannula at 30° angle, advance until blood flashback; advance further 2 mm; advance plastic cannula off needle into vessel.
steps.safetyCheck: Pulsatile bright-red blood confirms arterial.

steps.detail: Zero transducer at level of right atrium. Check waveform — dicrotic notch present, MAP makes sense.
Sutures + transparent dressing.

redFlags: Persistent loss of distal perfusion → REMOVE immediately.
Cold pulseless fingers → emergency vascular review.
Damped waveform / no flashback → line displaced / kinked / thrombosed.
postProcedureCare: Continuous transducer monitoring.
4-hourly distal limb assessment for ischaemia.
Daily review of need (remove ASAP).

complications.management: Remove line; warm; vascular consult if persistent ischaemia.
Direct pressure 5–10 min on removal.
Remove line; culture; antibiotic.

title: Nebuliser administration — bronchodilator / mucolytic
indications: Acute asthma / COPD exacerbation.
Croup (nebulised adrenaline / budesonide).
Cystic fibrosis (dornase, hypertonic saline).

relative: Cooperation issues (use spacer + pMDI alternative where possible).

equipment: Nebuliser chamber + mouthpiece (preferred) or face mask.
Oxygen flow 6–8 L/min (or compressed-air driver for COPD with hypercapnia risk).
consentNotes: Verbal consent.

steps.detail: OXYGEN for acute asthma + most paediatric uses. COMPRESSED AIR for COPD with type 2 respiratory failure / risk of hypercapnia (titrate supplementary oxygen separately to SpO₂ 88–92 %).
Combination chamber: salbutamol 2.5 or 5 mg + ipratropium 250 or 500 µg + saline up to 4–5 mL total volume.
Sitting upright. Mouthpiece between teeth, lips sealed. Mask if child / unable.
Tidal breathing through mouthpiece; complete in 10–15 min when chamber sputters / no further mist.
Pulse, RR, SpO₂, PEFR before + after.

redFlags: Tachycardia > 140 / min after salbutamol → check K+ + lactate; reduce frequency.
Failure to improve PEFR / SpO₂ → escalate to IV magnesium / IV salbutamol / ICU.
Worsening cough / paradoxical bronchospasm — rare; stop.
postProcedureCare: Counsel hand hygiene + spacer/inhaler review.
Rinse mouth after each nebulised steroid.

complications.management: Spread out doses; check K+ + replace.
Use mouthpiece not mask; treat with pilocarpine + ophthalmology.

title: Lumbar puncture — paediatric
indications: Suspected meningitis / encephalitis.
Investigation of unexplained seizures / encephalopathy.
Diagnostic for inborn errors of metabolism / leukaemia (CNS staging).

absolute: Signs of raised ICP / focal neurology / posturing.

equipment: Topical / infiltrative anaesthetic — EMLA or 1 % lidocaine.
consentNotes: Counsel parents: indication, common (post-LP headache rare in young children), serious risks (bleeding, herniation if raised ICP, infection). Document written consent.

steps.detail: Examination — no focal signs, no posturing, no irregular respirations / Cushing's triad.
steps.safetyCheck: If concerns: CT first.

steps.detail: EMLA 30–60 min pre-procedure where time allows.
Held lateral decubitus by experienced assistant: knees to chest, back curved. AVOID over-flexion in neonates (airway compromise).
Iliac-crest line crosses L4.
Iodine / chlorhexidine; sterile drape.
Bevel up, parallel to spine fibres. Advance slowly with stylet — feel 'pop' through ligamentum flavum then dural pop.
3 tubes ~ 0.5 mL each (1 mL in infants): biochemistry, microbiology, cytology. Send paired blood glucose. Opening pressure with manometer if able.

redFlags: Apnoea / desaturation during procedure → stop, support airway.
Bloody tap — distinguish traumatic vs SAH (third tube cell count, xanthochromia at 12 h).
Failed attempts × 3 — pause, reposition, consider ultrasound-guided or senior.
postProcedureCare: Apply small dressing.
Lay flat 1 h (controversial; less effective than once thought).
Document procedure + CSF appearance.

complications.management: Hydration + paracetamol + caffeine. Epidural blood patch if persistent.
Prevent by careful pre-procedure assessment. If suspected: intubate + hyperventilate + mannitol + neurosurgery.
Urgent MRI + neurosurgery.

references.label: WHO Pocket Book of Hospital Care for Children

title: Wound debridement — necrotic / contaminated wound
indications: Necrotic / devitalised tissue.
Heavily contaminated wound.
Diabetic foot ulcer with slough / necrosis.
Pressure ulcer with eschar / necrosis.

absolute: Dry stable eschar over ischaemic limb without infection — refer vascular first.

consentNotes: Counsel: pain, bleeding, scarring, may need repeat. Written consent for surgical debridement.

steps.detail: Identify viable vs non-viable tissue (colour, bleeding, capillary refill). Photograph + measure.
Local infiltration + topical lignocaine OR regional / general for extensive debridement.
Sharp excision of clearly necrotic tissue back to bleeding viable tissue. Preserve any tendon / bone / nerve until specialist.
Copious normal saline under pressure (50–100 mL/cm² of wound).
Moist (hydrocolloid / hydrogel / alginate per exudate) + antimicrobial (silver / iodine) if infected.

redFlags: Bone exposed / sequestrum → osteomyelitis workup + orthopaedic / ID.
Necrotising fasciitis features → SURGICAL EMERGENCY.
Persistent foul discharge / failure to heal → reassess; tissue biopsy + culture.
Critical limb ischaemia → vascular surgery.
postProcedureCare: Dressing changes 2–3 ×/week.
Off-loading (foot ulcer) — total contact cast / boot.
Address underlying cause (glycaemic control, vascular, pressure relief, nutrition).
Tetanus prophylaxis.

complications.management: Repeat surgical debridement.
Pressure, vascular surgery consult.

title: Neonatal resuscitation (Helping Babies Breathe)
indications: Newborn not breathing or not crying within the Golden Minute after birth.
Newborn with gasping respiration or HR < 100 bpm.

relative: Confirmed lethal congenital anomaly per local policy + senior + family decision.

equipment: Self-inflating bag-valve-mask (240/500 mL) + appropriate face masks (term + preterm).
consentNotes: Emergency — implied consent. Communicate clearly with mother / family during + after. Document timeline.

steps.detail: Identify a helper, check equipment, ensure warm room (25–28 °C), dry towels ready.
Dry thoroughly, remove wet cloth, keep warm. Stimulation by drying often initiates breathing.
If breathing well → routine care + skin-to-skin + delayed cord clamping (≥ 1 min). If not breathing / gasping → call for help + clear airway + start ventilation.
Position head neutral ('sniffing'). Suction mouth then nose only if secretions obstruct (avoid deep/vigorous suction — bradycardia).
Bag-mask ventilation 40–60 breaths/min with good seal + visible chest rise. Start with room air (term). The single most important intervention.

HR ≥ 100 + breathing → monitor. HR 60–99 → continue effective ventilation + correct technique (MR SOPA). HR < 60 despite 30 s effective ventilation → add chest compressions 3:1 + escalate + consider oxygen + adrenaline + senior.
Once stable: skin-to-skin, monitor breathing + temperature + colour, support breastfeeding, observe ≥ 1 h.

redFlags: HR remains < 60 despite effective ventilation + compressions.
No spontaneous breathing at 20 min of effective resuscitation (discuss stopping with senior).
Persistent central cyanosis / hypoxia.
Preterm / very low birth weight — escalate early.
postProcedureCare: Keep warm (prevent hypothermia — major killer).
Monitor breathing + HR + temperature + glucose.
Early breastfeeding.
Document Apgar + interventions + timeline.
Refer to neonatal unit if ongoing support needed.

complications.management: Skin-to-skin, hat, warm environment, monitor temperature.
Needle decompression + chest drain; gentle ventilation technique.
Therapeutic hypothermia where available; supportive neonatal intensive care.

references.label: WHO Helping Babies Breathe / Essential Newborn Care

title: Arthrocentesis (knee joint aspiration)
indications: Diagnostic — suspected septic arthritis (URGENT), crystal arthropathy (gout / pseudogout), undiagnosed effusion.
Therapeutic — drainage of tense haemarthrosis / large effusion for symptom relief.

absolute: Overlying cellulitis / skin infection at puncture site (seeds the joint).
relative: Prosthetic joint (refer orthopaedics — risk of prosthetic joint infection).

consentNotes: Counsel on indication, risk of infection (rare with sterile technique), bleeding, post-procedure discomfort. Document consent.

steps.detail: Inspect skin — no cellulitis. Identify the superolateral or medial patellar approach with knee slightly flexed.
Antiseptic skin prep, sterile drape, sterile gloves. Local anaesthetic to skin + track.
Insert needle at the chosen approach, aspirate steadily. Send fluid for urgent microscopy + Gram stain + culture + crystals + cell count.
Cloudy/purulent + high neutrophils → treat as septic arthritis until proven otherwise. Negatively birefringent needles → gout; positively birefringent rhomboids → pseudogout.

redFlags: Frank pus / very high synovial WCC → septic arthritis emergency: IV antibiotics + orthopaedic washout.
Fever + systemic upset.
Prosthetic joint involved.
postProcedureCare: Apply dressing. Rest joint briefly.
Chase culture + crystal results.
Start empirical IV antibiotics immediately if septic arthritis suspected (do not wait for culture).

complications.management: Strict asepsis prevents; if occurs → urgent washout + IV antibiotics.
Pressure, correct coagulopathy.

title: Synchronised DC cardioversion
indications: Unstable tachyarrhythmia with a pulse (AF, atrial flutter, SVT, VT) + adverse features — shock, syncope, myocardial ischaemia, heart failure.
Elective cardioversion of persistent AF / flutter (anticoagulated / TOE-guided).

absolute: Pulseless VT/VF → use UNsynchronised defibrillation instead.
Digoxin toxicity (relative — risk of malignant arrhythmia).
relative: AF > 48 h without anticoagulation / TOE (thromboembolism risk) unless unstable.

equipment: Defibrillator with SYNC mode + ECG leads.
Sedation / anaesthesia (e.g. propofol / etomidate + airway support).
Oxygen, suction, BVM, monitoring (ECG, SpO₂, BP).
consentNotes: If time permits, counsel on procedure, sedation risks, need for anticoagulation, recurrence. Emergency = implied consent if unstable.

steps.step: Confirm SYNC mode is ON + a pulse is present
steps.detail: Verify the defibrillator marks the R waves (sync markers) before charging. Cardioverting a pulseless rhythm or syncing incorrectly can induce VF.
Anaesthetic / sedation with airway support. Continuous ECG + SpO₂ + BP. Pre-oxygenate.
Energy: AF 120–150 J biphasic; atrial flutter / SVT 70–120 J; VT with pulse 120–150 J. Charge, ensure 'all clear', deliver. Re-confirm sync between shocks (machine often reverts to defib mode).
Check rhythm + pulse. If unsuccessful, escalate energy + repeat (max 3 attempts then expert help + treat reversible causes / consider amiodarone).

redFlags: Deterioration to VF (re-confirm SYNC was on).
Failure after 3 shocks — seek cardiology + treat electrolytes.
Post-cardioversion thromboembolism / stroke.
postProcedureCare: Monitor rhythm + recovery from sedation.
Continue / start anticoagulation per CHA₂DS₂-VASc.
12-lead ECG. Identify + treat the precipitant.
Cardiology follow-up.

complications.management: Immediate unsynchronised defibrillation + ALS.
Anticoagulation per protocol; TOE-guidance for AF > 48 h.
Use gel pads, good contact.

references.label: Resuscitation Council UK Peri-arrest Tachycardia Algorithm

title: Anterior nasal packing for epistaxis
indications: Anterior epistaxis not controlled by first-aid (pinch + lean forward) + cautery.
Ongoing bleeding requiring tamponade.

absolute: Suspected basal skull fracture / CSF rhinorrhoea (nasal packing contraindicated — neurosurgery).

equipment: Nasal tampon (Merocel/Rapid Rhino) or ribbon gauze + BIPP.
consentNotes: Explain discomfort, need to keep pack in 24–48 h, possible re-bleed, removal plan. Document.

steps.detail: Apply PPE. Assess for shock (large-volume bleed) + secure IV access + bloods/group-save if heavy. Exclude posterior bleed (bleeding down throat despite anterior pack).
Suction clots. Apply topical vasoconstrictor + anaesthetic on a pledget for several minutes.

steps.step: Attempt cautery if a discrete vessel seen
steps.detail: Silver nitrate cautery to Little's area (one side of septum only — avoid septal perforation). If diffuse / unsuccessful, pack.
Insert tampon along the floor of the nose (not upward), parallel to the hard palate. Expand (wet Merocel / inflate Rapid Rhino). If still bleeding, pack the other nostril.
Check no ongoing bleeding anteriorly or posteriorly. Examine throat.

redFlags: Bleeding continues despite bilateral anterior packing → posterior bleed: posterior pack / Foley + urgent ENT.
Haemodynamic instability.
Anticoagulation / coagulopathy.
Recurrent epistaxis — investigate (HHT, malignancy, hypertension).
postProcedureCare: Admit if elderly / heavy bleed / posterior pack / comorbidity.
Antibiotic prophylaxis for packs in situ > 48 h (toxic shock risk).
Pack removal 24–48 h. ENT follow-up for recurrent.
Address BP + anticoagulation + reversal as needed.

complications.management: Antibiotic prophylaxis; remove pack within 48 h.
Cauterise one side only.
Posterior packing + ENT + airway support.

title: Reduction of anterior shoulder dislocation
indications: Confirmed anterior glenohumeral dislocation.

absolute: Associated displaced fracture requiring surgery (discuss orthopaedics before reduction).
relative: Neurovascular compromise — reduce promptly but document first.
Posterior dislocation (different technique — often needs imaging + senior).

equipment: Analgesia + sedation (e.g. opioid ± procedural sedation) or intra-articular lignocaine.
Pillow / broad arm sling for post-reduction.
consentNotes: Counsel on reduction, sedation risks, possibility of fracture / failure / recurrent instability. Document neurovascular status.

steps.step: Document neurovascular status + confirm dislocation on X-ray
steps.detail: Assess axillary nerve (regimental badge sensation + deltoid), radial/median/ulnar function, distal pulses BEFORE + AFTER reduction. Confirm anterior dislocation + exclude fracture on pre-reduction film.
Adequate analgesia ± procedural sedation, OR intra-articular lignocaine 20 mL 1% (avoids sedation risks). Monitor if sedated.
Use a low-force technique — scapular manipulation, external rotation (Cunningham), or Stimson (prone with weight). Avoid forceful traction-countertraction (fracture risk).
Clinical 'clunk' + restored contour + improved pain. Post-reduction X-ray to confirm + exclude fracture.

redFlags: Neurovascular deficit pre or post reduction → senior + vascular/ortho.
Associated fracture (greater tuberosity, Bankart, Hill-Sachs).
Irreducible dislocation → theatre.
First dislocation in young patient — high recurrence.
postProcedureCare: Broad arm sling 1–3 weeks (balance immobilisation vs stiffness).
Re-document neurovascular status.
Orthopaedic / physiotherapy follow-up. Early mobilisation in elderly to avoid frozen shoulder.

complications.management: Usually neuropraxia — document, physiotherapy, monitor recovery.
Gentle technique prevents; orthopaedic referral.
Physiotherapy; surgical stabilisation if recurrent + young.

title: Closed reduction of distal radius (Colles) fracture
indications: Displaced / angulated distal radius fracture requiring reduction before casting.

relative: Significant comminution (likely to re-displace — discuss orthopaedics).

equipment: Analgesia — haematoma block (lignocaine into fracture site) or Bier's block or procedural sedation.
consentNotes: Counsel on reduction, anaesthetic method, risk of re-displacement / need for surgery, compartment syndrome warning. Document neurovascular status.

steps.step: Document neurovascular status + median nerve function
steps.detail: Check median nerve (thumb sensation + abduction), radial/ulnar, capillary refill, before + after. Confirm fracture pattern on X-ray.
Haematoma block: 10 mL 1% lignocaine into the fracture haematoma under aseptic technique; wait 10 min. Alternative: Bier's block / sedation.
Apply traction (finger traps useful), then disimpact + reverse the deformity (correct dorsal angulation + radial shift). Maintain reduction while applying backslab.
Apply a dorsal below-elbow backslab (NOT a full circumferential cast acutely — swelling). Re-X-ray to confirm acceptable alignment.

redFlags: Median nerve symptoms (acute carpal tunnel) → urgent decompression / senior.
Increasing pain + tense swelling → compartment syndrome.
Unacceptable reduction → orthopaedic referral for fixation.
postProcedureCare: Backslab + high arm sling + elevation.
Compartment-syndrome safety-net advice (severe pain, numbness, tightness — return immediately).
Fracture clinic in 1 week for cast completion + repeat X-ray.
Re-document neurovascular status.

complications.management: Avoid circumferential cast acutely; split cast; fasciotomy if confirmed.
Urgent decompression.
Repeat reduction or surgical fixation.

title: Plaster backslab application
indications: Immobilisation of an acute fracture / soft-tissue injury where swelling is expected (backslab allows expansion, unlike circumferential cast).
equipment: Plaster of Paris or fibreglass slab.
consentNotes: Explain purpose, need to keep dry, elevation, safety-net for compartment syndrome. Document.

steps.step: Assess + document neurovascular status before applying
steps.detail: Check distal pulses, sensation, movement, capillary refill. Re-check after application.
Stockinette over the limb, then even wool padding (extra over bony prominences). No wrinkles.
Measure + wet the slab, smooth out, position over the limb on the appropriate side, mould to the desired position while setting. Hold the joint in the functional / reduced position.
Bandage (not too tight). Confirm the slab is NOT circumferential (allows swelling). Re-check neurovascular status.

redFlags: Increasing pain / tightness / numbness → compartment syndrome — split + open the slab immediately.
Loss of distal pulses / cold limb.
Cast too tight.
postProcedureCare: Elevate limb. High arm sling for upper limb.
Compartment-syndrome + cast-care safety-net advice (keep dry, don't insert objects, return if pain/numbness).
Fracture clinic follow-up.
Convert to full cast when swelling settles (~1 week).

complications.management: Split cast full length to skin; fasciotomy if confirmed.
Adequate padding over prominences.
Use lukewarm water; counsel patient.

title: Digital (ring) nerve block
indications: Anaesthesia of a finger / toe for laceration repair, nail procedures, foreign body removal, fracture/dislocation reduction.
equipment: 1% or 2% plain lignocaine (traditionally WITHOUT adrenaline — see note).
consentNotes: Explain transient pain on injection, expected numbness, duration. Document.

steps.step: Confirm intact digital circulation + no infection
steps.detail: Check capillary refill + colour. Avoid in an already-ischaemic digit. (Modern evidence supports low-dose adrenaline as safe in healthy digits, but plain lignocaine remains the cautious default.)
Clean the base of the digit. Identify the two dorsal + two palmar/plantar digital nerves at the web spaces.

At the base of the digit, insert dorsally on each side, aspirate, then inject ~1–1.5 mL each side advancing toward the palmar surface. Total ≤ 4 mL. Avoid circumferential ring infiltration under high pressure (tourniquet effect).
Allow 5–10 min. Test sensation before starting the procedure.

redFlags: Pallor / loss of capillary refill after injection → remove pressure, do not use excessive volume.
Signs of infection.
Failure of block — top up or alternative.
postProcedureCare: Counsel that numbness lasts a few hours — protect the digit.
Standard wound / procedure aftercare.

complications.management: Avoid excessive volume + high-pressure ring infiltration; treat as ischaemia if occurs.
Aspirate before injecting; Intralipid for systemic toxicity.

title: Ear irrigation (cerumen removal)
indications: Symptomatic impacted earwax (hearing loss, discomfort) after softening drops, where microsuction unavailable.

absolute: Perforated tympanic membrane / current or recent ear infection.

equipment: Electronic irrigator with controlled pressure (NOT a metal syringe — pressure injury risk).
consentNotes: Explain procedure, transient dizziness, small risk of perforation / infection / pain. Confirm no contraindication. Document.

steps.step: Otoscopy first — confirm intact eardrum + no infection
steps.detail: Examine both ears. Do NOT irrigate if perforation, infection, or contraindication present. Confirm wax (not a foreign body / keratosis).
Olive oil / sodium bicarbonate drops for 3–5 days improves success + safety.
Body-temperature water (cold/hot causes vertigo). Pull pinna up + back (adult). Direct the stream along the postero-superior canal wall, not at the drum. Use controlled low pressure.
Stop if pain / dizziness / discharge. Otoscope to confirm clearance + intact drum afterwards.

redFlags: Pain / bleeding / discharge during procedure → stop + examine for perforation.
Vertigo (water temperature).
Foreign body that could swell (organic) — refer.
postProcedureCare: Dry the ear. Advise against cotton buds.
Review hearing. Refer ENT if persistent symptoms / suspected perforation.

complications.management: Stop; keep dry; antibiotic drops if infected; ENT referral.
Dry ear; topical antibiotic-steroid.
Use body-temperature water; let patient recover.

references.label: NICE NG98 Hearing Loss / CKS Earwax

title: Corneal / conjunctival foreign body removal
indications: Superficial corneal or conjunctival foreign body.

absolute: Suspected penetrating / intra-ocular foreign body or globe rupture (do NOT manipulate — shield + urgent ophthalmology).
Deeply embedded / central visual-axis foreign body — refer.

equipment: Sterile 25 G needle or cotton bud / foreign-body spud.
consentNotes: Explain procedure, possibility of residual rust ring, need for follow-up, risks. Document visual acuity first.

steps.step: Check visual acuity + exclude penetrating injury
steps.detail: Document acuity in each eye. High-velocity mechanism (grinding/hammering) → suspect intraocular FB → X-ray/CT + ophthalmology, do NOT probe. Seidel test if globe rupture suspected.
Topical anaesthetic. Examine under magnification + fluorescein. Evert the upper lid to check for sub-tarsal FB.
Loose FB — irrigate or lift with a moist cotton bud. Adherent corneal FB — lift gently with the bevel of a 25 G needle tangential to the cornea under magnification (slit lamp ideal).
Metallic FB leaves a rust ring — may need a burr / ophthalmology. Apply topical antibiotic. Re-stain to assess the epithelial defect.

redFlags: High-velocity mechanism / suspected penetrating injury → shield eye + urgent ophthalmology, do not manipulate.
Central / deep FB.
Worsening pain / vision / photophobia after removal (infection / ulcer).
postProcedureCare: Topical antibiotic (e.g. chloramphenicol) several days.
Analgesia. AVOID topical anaesthetic for ongoing pain (toxic to epithelium).
Review in 24–48 h; ophthalmology if not healing / rust ring / large defect.

complications.management: Topical antibiotics + urgent ophthalmology.
Burr removal / ophthalmology.
High index of suspicion; imaging; ophthalmology.

title: Ingrowing toenail — partial nail avulsion + phenolisation
indications: Recurrent / infected ingrowing toenail (onychocryptosis) failing conservative care.

absolute: Critical limb ischaemia (poor healing — vascular review).
relative: Poorly-controlled diabetes / peripheral vascular disease — caution + foot team.

equipment: Phenol 80% + cotton buds (for matrixectomy) + alcohol/saline to neutralise.
consentNotes: Explain partial nail removal, phenol to prevent regrowth, narrower nail appearance, healing weeks, recurrence + infection risk. Check vascular + diabetic status. Document.

steps.step: Assess distal circulation + diabetic/vascular status before block + tourniquet
steps.detail: Confirm adequate perfusion. A digital tourniquet on an ischaemic toe risks necrosis. Mark + confirm the correct toe.
Plain lignocaine ring block; wait for anaesthesia. Apply a digital tourniquet (note time).
Free the lateral nail edge with an elevator, split longitudinally with nippers, remove the ingrowing portion including the buried spike.
Apply 80% phenol to the exposed germinal matrix for ~1–3 min (prevents regrowth), then neutralise thoroughly with alcohol/saline. Avoid spread to healthy tissue.
Non-adherent dressing. Release the tourniquet + confirm perfusion returns.

redFlags: Spreading cellulitis / systemic infection.
Ischaemia after tourniquet.
Diabetic foot — low threshold for foot-team referral.
postProcedureCare: Elevate. Simple analgesia. Daily salt-water soaks + dressing changes.
Keep dressing dry initially; review for healing.
Footwear advice; correct nail-cutting technique to prevent recurrence.

complications.management: Antibiotics; dressing; review.
Neutralise thoroughly; protect surrounding skin.
Repeat / definitive matrixectomy.

title: Skin punch biopsy
indications: Diagnostic sampling of an undiagnosed rash / lesion; suspected inflammatory dermatosis; ruling out malignancy (non-excisional).

absolute: Suspected melanoma where a punch may under-sample — excisional biopsy preferred (refer).

equipment: Local anaesthetic (lignocaine + adrenaline, except acral sites).
consentNotes: Explain small scar, bleeding, infection, that it may not give a complete diagnosis. Document site (photo / diagram).

steps.step: Confirm site + mark + photograph; reconsider if melanoma suspected
steps.detail: Mark the most representative area (edge of an active lesion). If melanoma is a possibility, refer for EXCISIONAL biopsy rather than punch.
Clean. Infiltrate local anaesthetic (avoid adrenaline on digits/penis/ear/nose tip).
Stretch skin perpendicular to relaxed skin tension lines. Press + rotate the punch to the dermis/fat. Lift the core with forceps (handle gently — avoid crush) + cut the base.
Suture (≥ 4 mm) or haemostatic dressing. Place specimen in formalin, label correctly, complete the histology request with clinical details.

redFlags: Suspected melanoma — do not punch; refer for excision.
Site bleeding (correct coagulopathy).
Signs of infection at follow-up.
postProcedureCare: Keep dry 24–48 h. Suture removal 5–14 days by site.
Safety-net for infection. Arrange histology follow-up + communicate results.

complications.management: Repeat / excisional biopsy.
Antibiotics; dressing.
Counsel; minimise tension.

title: Episiotomy + repair
indications: Mediolateral episiotomy when needed to expedite delivery — fetal compromise, instrumental delivery, imminent severe tear, shoulder dystocia.
NOT routine (restrictive use reduces severe perineal trauma).
equipment: Local anaesthetic (lignocaine) if not already epidural/pudendal.
consentNotes: Where possible counsel during labour. Explain indication, repair, analgesia, healing, risk of extension to higher-degree tear. Document.

steps.step: Confirm indication + adequate analgesia + correct angle
steps.detail: Only cut for a clear indication. Ensure perineal anaesthesia. Make a MEDIOLATERAL incision (60° from the midline at crowning) to reduce risk of anal sphincter injury.
Single deliberate cut at the height of a contraction when the perineum is distended + the head crowns.
After delivery + placenta, examine systematically (including a per-rectal exam) to grade any tear + exclude obstetric anal sphincter injury (OASI). OASI → repair by trained clinician in theatre.
Repair vaginal mucosa (continuous), perineal muscle (interrupted/continuous), then skin (subcuticular). Count swabs + needles. Achieve haemostasis.

redFlags: Third/fourth-degree tear (OASI) → trained repair in theatre.
Ongoing bleeding / haematoma.
Swab/needle count incorrect.
Rectal mucosa involvement.
postProcedureCare: Analgesia (paracetamol + NSAID), ice, hygiene.
Laxative + advise against straining (especially after OASI).
Watch for infection / breakdown / haematoma.
Pelvic-floor physiotherapy; follow-up especially after OASI.

complications.management: Trained repair in theatre; physiotherapy; follow-up.
Antibiotics; wound care; resuture if needed.
Evacuate + secure haemostasis.

title: Vacuum-assisted (ventouse) delivery
indications: Prolonged second stage, fetal compromise in the second stage, or maternal exhaustion — with a fully dilated cervix + engaged head + known position.

absolute: Gestation < 34 weeks (fetal scalp fragility) — relative/absolute by device.
relative: After failed forceps (or vice versa — avoid sequential instruments).

consentNotes: Counsel on indication, alternatives (forceps / caesarean), maternal + neonatal risks, possibility of failure → caesarean. Document.

steps.step: Confirm prerequisites + bladder empty + correct cup placement
steps.detail: Verify FORCEPS mnemonic prerequisites: Fully dilated, OA position known, Cephalic, Engaged, Pain relief, Sphincter (bladder) empty. Place the cup over the flexion point (3 cm anterior to the posterior fontanelle). Senior present.
